note: C13-4 seed scene cards (report 1 P1-2): expected flow, register, key chunks and one small surprise for each of the 36 seeds. Written by an AI assistant as synthetic product design; not yet reviewed by a local reviewer.

flow: The teacher greets the parent and introduces themself as the form teacher
The parent introduces themself and their child
The parent says they are still learning English and asks the teacher to speak slowly
The teacher agrees and checks the best way to talk
S01.twist: The teacher has only five minutes before the next class.

flow: The parent asks how the child is doing in class
The teacher shares one observation about understanding
The parent asks what to watch out for
The teacher gives one simple tip
S02.twist: The school bell rings and the teacher has to leave soon.

flow: The parent asks how to help at home
The teacher suggests one simple activity
The parent repeats it to check
The teacher confirms and says how often
S03.twist: The parent cannot read the English worksheets well.

flow: The parent asks how to keep in touch
The teacher offers a message or a call
The parent explains they work during the day
They agree on a way and a time
S04.twist: The phone number in the school letter is out of date.

flow: The parent asks how the child is settling in
The teacher describes the first weeks
The parent asks one question about friends or lessons
The teacher suggests checking again in a few weeks
S05.twist: The child will have a different form teacher from next week.

flow: The parent asks about the school day
The teacher explains the arrival and recess times
The parent asks about lunch and dismissal
The teacher confirms the pick-up point
S06.twist: On Wednesdays the child stays back for CCA.

flow: The parent says the child feels alone at school
The teacher shares what they have seen
They talk about one way to help
The teacher offers to check in with the child
S07.twist: The teacher has noticed the child sits with one classmate at recess.

flow: The teacher asks about the child
The parent shares what the child likes and is good at
The parent mentions one area that needs support
The teacher thanks them and notes it down
S08.twist: The teacher asks for an example the parent did not prepare.

flow: The parent says the child had a problem with a classmate
The parent shares what the child said
The teacher says what they saw
They agree on a next step
S09.twist: The teacher did not see what happened and needs to ask others.

flow: The parent mentions the last talk
The teacher gives a short update
They agree how to follow up
They set the next date to talk
S10.twist: The teacher will be away, so another teacher will reply.

flow: The parent raises screen time at home
The teacher asks how long the child uses devices
The teacher shares a school suggestion
The parent says what they will try
S11.twist: The child also needs the tablet for homework.

flow: The parent says the child got upsetting messages online
The teacher listens and asks when it happened
The teacher explains the support the school can give
They agree on who to contact next
S12.twist: The messages came from a group chat outside school.

flow: The supervisor gives quick instructions
The worker asks them to slow down
The supervisor repeats more slowly
The worker repeats the key point
S13.twist: The supervisor is called away halfway through.

flow: The supervisor lists a few tasks
The worker asks which one comes first
The supervisor gives the order
The worker repeats the order to check
S14.twist: One task becomes urgent while they are talking.

flow: A colleague explains what to watch on the next shift
The worker repeats the points back
The colleague corrects one detail
The worker confirms
S15.twist: One machine needs checking every hour, not every two hours.

flow: The supervisor explains a safety rule
The worker says they did not understand
The worker asks to pause and hear it again
The supervisor shows or explains it simply
S16.twist: The rule uses a word the worker has never heard.

flow: The worker asks about one item on the payslip
A colleague explains what it is
The worker asks one follow-up question
The colleague says who to ask if unsure
S17.twist: The colleague is not sure and suggests asking the HR office.

flow: The worker says they worked overtime last week
The supervisor checks the record
The worker confirms the dates and hours
The supervisor says when it will be updated
S18.twist: One day is missing from the record.

flow: The worker explains the problem
A colleague suggests the right person
The worker asks how to contact them
The colleague gives a simple way
S19.twist: The person in charge is on leave today.

flow: The worker says the document is hard to follow
The worker asks for simpler English
The person in charge explains the main point
The worker asks if there is a version in another language
S20.twist: There is no translated version, but there is a picture guide.

flow: The receptionist answers the phone
The caller asks for an appointment
The receptionist offers some times
The caller chooses one and gives a name
S21.twist: Only walk-in queue numbers are left for today.

flow: The caller says the booked time is not convenient
The receptionist asks for the name and date
The receptionist offers other afternoons
The caller confirms the new time
S22.twist: The doctor is only in on Thursday afternoons.

flow: The patient asks where the clinic is
The receptionist gives the level and room
The patient asks what to bring
The receptionist lists the items and when to arrive
S23.twist: The lift to that level is under repair.

flow: The patient says the booking does not show online
The receptionist checks the system
The receptionist explains what happened
They fix it or book again
S24.twist: The booking was made under a family member's name.

flow: The commuter tells the staff the gate did not open
The staff asks to see the card
The staff explains the problem
The staff says what to do next
S25.twist: The card works, but it was tapped twice.

flow: The staff says to go to the service point
The commuter asks where it is
The staff gives simple directions
The commuter repeats them
S26.twist: The service centre closes in ten minutes.

flow: The commuter says one fare was higher than usual
The staff asks about the trip
The staff explains how to check the record
The commuter asks one more question
S27.twist: The commuter forgot to tap out at the end of the trip.

flow: The staff explains something quickly
The commuter says they did not catch it
The staff says it again more simply
The commuter checks they understood
chunks: Sorry, can you say that again slowly?
S28.twist: The staff uses a station name the commuter has not heard.

flow: The neighbour greets the resident in the corridor
The resident introduces themself
They share a little about their families
They say goodbye kindly
S29.twist: The neighbour asks whether the resident has a pet.

flow: The resident says water is dripping from the ceiling
The neighbour upstairs listens
The resident asks to check it together
They agree on a time
S30.twist: The neighbour upstairs is renting and must ask the owner first.

flow: The contractor calls about the visit
The resident asks what time
The contractor explains the work
The resident explains nobody is home during the day
S31.twist: The contractor can only come on a weekday morning.

flow: The resident greets the neighbour
The resident gently mentions the noise at night
The neighbour responds
They agree on one idea together
S32.twist: The neighbour did not know the noise could be heard downstairs.

flow: The stall assistant asks what to drink
The customer orders a kopi
The assistant asks about sugar or ice
The customer answers and pays
S33.twist: The assistant asks quickly whether it is kopi-O or kopi-C.

flow: The customer orders a tea
The assistant asks about sweetness
The customer asks for less sugar and ice
The assistant repeats the order
S34.twist: The iced drink costs a little more than the hot one.

flow: The stall owner asks what the customer wants
The customer orders
The owner asks whether to eat here or take away
The customer answers and pays
S35.twist: The owner asks the customer to wait for a new tray of food.

flow: The assistant uses a local word
The customer asks what it means
The assistant explains it simply
The customer confirms the order
S36.twist: The word sounds like the name of another drink.
